In 2013, we were introduced through a mutual acquaintance of President Kim of Orgiast (オージャスト), and our relationship began when we started providing sales support, a service of our company. After that, there was a gap, and then again just before our listing in 2021, we were introduced by another person. They said, 'If you are going to hold a listing commemorative party, I will introduce you to a good company.'

Since an initial public offering is not something one experiences often among corporate events, we wanted to show our gratitude, especially to the employees who had advanced with us and to our partners. We considered various initiatives, and decided that holding a listing commemorative party with a certain budget was the best option, so we decided to hold it. We conveyed the concept of a 'Thank You Festival for Employees' to Orgiast (オージャスト) and requested them to plan it.
―――There are other companies that hold internal events, but why did you choose to request this from Orgiast (オージャスト)?

After all, we had known them for a long time, and the fact that they have a lot of track record was a major reason. There were sales approaches from other companies, but it wasn't something to put out to competition. Since we had little experience using event companies, I think we would have done it in-house if we hadn't requested Orgiast (オージャスト).
―――In what areas did you feel it was good to leave it to Orgiast (オージャスト)?

The fact that they made proposals from our company's standpoint. While we had some desires on our part, there were times when we had conflicts with Orgiast's (オージャスト) proposals. In such situations, they not only shaped our wishes as they were, but also gave us advice from the standpoint of a knowledgeable professional, saying, 'To realize the concept, wouldn't it be better to do it this way?' That led to trust.
―――Are there any events you would like to implement together with Orgiast (オージャスト) in the future?

Currently, including contract workers, we have about 3,000 people, but we aim to create employment for about 10,000 people in 2023. We are thinking of holding a grand event to commemorate that. We would definitely like Orgiast (オージャスト) to cooperate again.

This time, we spoke with Representative Director Mr. Tariki (他力野) of Value Management Co., Ltd. about the introduction of an in-home assistant system.
Orgiast (オージャスト) was different in their approach; they read the intention and meaning of what we wanted to do, incorporated that, and provided management through detailed task administration.
Orgiast's (オージャスト) method was completely different, and I was surprised that they work with such excitement.
> I imagine you were surprised by the 'no management' aspect. What are your personal impressions of this introduction, President Tariki (他力野)?

To that end, we asked the freelancers to work with us, and they agreed. At Orgiast (オージャスト), it's a model where freelancers work together, right? That foundation was laid first, and we actually saw the deliverables. We felt a sense of effectiveness, thinking, 'This can work,' so we are promoting it.
> Now that you have become a business partner based on a foundation of trust with Orgiast (オージャスト), are there any points where you truly feel it was good to leave it to Orgiast (オージャスト)?
Orgiast (オージャスト) is different from us; the fundamental premise is that they outsource everything.

We have an organization and are cutting out a part of it, we are still in that state. But Orgiast (オージャスト) competes with just that alone, so I think the system is built on the premise of rapid delivery.

They are doing this as a normal operation, so for us, this is still like an entry model, a part of it. Since we are mainly cutting out parts that are easy to separate, our next challenge is to outsource a core part. But Orgiast (オージャスト) has already outsourced their entire core, so the hurdle for us is still lower.

When we partially borrowed the system of Orgiast (オージャスト), which operates with its entire core outsourced, there was almost no stress during our introduction because the system's completeness was already high.
> You had a network foundation through new opportunities. Do you have any requests for Orgiast (オージャスト)?
Yes, I've also mentioned this to Mr. Kim (金), but I feel it's a waste.

I once directly told them, 'Isn't it a waste to keep it only within Orgiast (オージャスト)? This system should definitely be released externally.' I think it's that good of a system, so I really hope they do it.

However, I don't think it's easy. Most company presidents probably don't even have the concept. So, if Orgiast (オージャスト) communicates why it is valuable, and how to specifically achieve it, leading to various companies being able to introduce this system, it would be beneficial. In Japan, the labor force and working population are declining, so we need to consider more efficient ways of working as a nation. I hope this system spreads throughout Japan.

"Shanai Event Plus (社内イベントプラス)" - Custom-made In-house Events

A fact-finding survey was conducted targeting 110 individuals responsible for organizing general meetings of employees (社員総会) at companies that have held such meetings for at least three years, regarding the issue of such meetings becoming routine and stale (マンネリ化).

The more frequently general meetings of employees are held, the more the content tends to become the same each year, suggesting that the staleness experienced by those responsible, and of course by employees, progresses annually. Despite many people feeling this staleness, the reasons for the content becoming repetitive are thought to include the difficulty for those responsible in allocating time, budget issues, and a shortage of personnel. It appears that even if they want to make some change, it is difficult to actually do so. From this, it can be inferred that while many companies execute their general meetings of employees entirely in-house, there may be a need to leverage external expertise to succeed with a fully in-house approach. Creating a unique, company-original plan with professional assistance can significantly reduce the burden on those responsible, and consequently, it is expected that an internal meeting (社内総会) that all employees can look forward to enjoying could also lead to improved employee productivity.
